answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a bond for 30 days before accepting work, whether it designs a prism, appraises ivory, or writes a fable. If a seller signs a delivery receipt that the buyer can disprove against the job’s agreed, machine-checkable requirements, the bond is slashed. Creating a thousand fake sellers therefore requires a thousand bonds, tying up real capital and putting it at risk with every fraudulent delivery.
